advisory.checklist_item: - [ ] Make gc-config's gc.auto probe and unset use the same scope (`--local`), or stop letting a failed unset skip the autoDetach writes, so a gc.auto set outside the local config does not make the unit fail on every sweep
evidence: src/rebar/_commands/_init_ensures.py:77: `if _git(tracker, "config", "--get", "gc.auto").returncode == 0:` (no `--local`, so it reads system/global/local plus GIT_CONFIG_* env)

src/rebar/_commands/_init_ensures.py:78-79: `if failed := _write_failure("gc-config", _git(tracker, "config", "--unset", "gc.auto")): return failed` (an early return before the loop at line 81 that sets the autoDetach keys)

src/rebar/_store/gitutil.py:331-334: `git config` is exempt from the maintenance-off env injection ('its reads must show stored settings'), so an inherited GIT_CONFIG_COUNT/gc.auto in the caller's env is visible to `--get`
Before this change the unset result was ignored (`_git(tracker, "config", "--unset", "gc.auto")`), so the loop still wrote gc.autoDetach=false and maintenance.autoDetach=false
`git config --unset` without a scope edits only the repo-local file. It exits 5 when the key is absent there, which matches no case in _write_failure, so the result is reported as failed
advisory.finding: _gc_config_unit now returns `failed` as soon as `git config --unset gc.auto` fails. That command fails every time when gc.auto comes from global/system config or an inherited GIT_CONFIG_* env, because `--get` reads every scope while `--unset` only edits the local repo config. In that case the unit never sets gc.autoDetach or maintenance.autoDetach (which it did before this change), reports `failed` on every sweep and at the bootstrap pin, and is never written to `.ensure-applied`.
scenarios: A developer or CI host has `gc.auto` in ~/.gitconfig: every `rebar init`, MCP boot and `fsck --repair` warns `ensure 'gc-config' failed: ... exit 5`, and the detach safety net is never applied to the tracker
The pending-ensure write-path hint keeps naming gc-config because it never reaches `.ensure-applied`, and `fsck --repair` cannot converge it

test_the_next_sweep_converges_the_units_a_timeout_skipped asserts that every registry id is applied, so it would fail on a host whose global git config sets gc.auto, unless the test environment isolates HOME
advisory.suggested_fix: Probe with `_git(tracker, "config", "--local", "--get", "gc.auto")` so only a locally stored gc.auto triggers the unset. Alternatively, record the unset failure but keep going through the autoDetach loop and return `failed` at the end.

advisory.checklist_item: - [ ] Replace the os.path.exists check with `assert ensures.applied_ids(tracker) == set(ensures.REGISTRY_IDS) - {"gitattributes"}`
evidence: src/rebar/_commands/init.py:180,215,601,621: init calls `_run_ensures_logged(tracker, silent)`, which runs run_ensures and writes the marker before the test body starts

src/rebar/_store/ensures.py (diff): `_write_applied(tracker, [o.id for o in outcomes if o.status != "failed"])` is now fed by the new `_run_units`, so excluding failed units is behaviour this refactor must keep
advisory.finding: The final assertion of test_any_other_unit_error_is_still_recorded_and_the_sweep_continues only checks that the `.ensure-applied` file exists. The `tracker` fixture has already written that file by running init, so the check passes whatever this sweep does. Nothing checks that the failed `gitattributes` unit is left out of the applied set.
scenarios: A later change to _run_units or the applied-marker write wrongly records the failed unit, or writes nothing. The assertion still passes because init already created the file.

advisory.checklist_item: - [ ] Compute the expected skipped count from `len(ensures.REGISTRY_IDS) - 2` instead of the literal 8
evidence: tests/unit/test_ensure_git_timeout.py:108: `assert "config --get" in gc.detail and "8 later unit(s) not run" in gc.detail`
advisory.finding: test_the_sweep_stops_at_a_timeout_and_claims_no_later_unit hard-codes the count of skipped units as `8`. That number is just the registry size minus two. Registering a new ensure unit would break the test even though the timeout behaviour is unchanged.
scenarios: A developer registers an 11th ensure unit as docs/migrations.md step 2 describes, and this timeout test fails with nothing about timeouts having changed.
advisory.suggested_fix: assert f"{len(ensures.REGISTRY_IDS) - 2} later unit(s) not run" in gc.detail

advisory.checklist_item: - [ ] Add a test that seeds a tracked `.archived` marker, stubs `init._git` to return code 124 for `commit` (and, separately, for `rm`), and asserts GitTimedOut is raised
evidence: tests/unit/test_ensure_git_timeout.py:135-136: the stub only times out `args[:1] == ("ls-files",)`; rm and commit run for real
Searching tests for `_untrack_runtime_markers_unit` turns up only tests/unit/test_ensures_untrack_markers.py (pre-existing, no timeout stubbing) and this file
advisory.finding: The diff adds a timeout raise around each `rm --cached` batch and around the `commit` in `_untrack_runtime_markers_unit`, but only the `ls-files` timeout is tested. Nothing checks that a timed-out rm or commit raises GitTimedOut instead of returning `changed`.
scenarios: A store with tracked `.archived` markers, where `git commit` returns 124. If someone drops the commit wrapper, the unit reports 'changed: untracked N runtime marker file(s)' for a commit that never happened, and no test fails.
